links.comparator_used: Standard pre-trained LLM chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini) answering from training knowledge, compared with RAG-based Perplexity Pro; zero-shot protocol on 11 concussion queries
links.outcome: Reliability and information quality of concussion advice (DISCERN, EQIP), scored by two blinded neurosurgeons against the 2023 Amsterdam Consensus Statement
links.effect: Perplexity Pro DISCERN 47.36 ± 4.84 and EQIP 65.00 ± 5.48, higher than ChatGPT and Gemini (p < 0.01); DISCERN and EQIP differed across models (p < 0.001). GQS did not differ significantly (p = 0.373).
links.tradeoff: JAMA transparency stayed uniformly low across all models (p < 0.001). All models exceeded the 6th-grade reading level, and most exceeded 10th-grade; Perplexity Pro was lowest at FKGL = 7.46. The RAG attribution is inferred ("likely") from a cross-platform comparison, not an isolated ablation. Human-in-the-loop verification is advised.
links.quote: Perplexity Pro secured the highest DISCERN (47.36 ± 4.84) and EQIP (65.00 ± 5.48) values, statistically surpassing foundational models like ChatGPT and Gemini (p < 0.01) - a performance gap likely driven by its RAG design.
